about.title: Morgan Hill Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Morgan Hill's mix of agriculture, warehousing, construction and light industry along corridors like Monterey Road and Butterfield Boulevard means workplace injuries here often involve heavy equipment, vehicles, or third-party contractors moving through busy job sites. When you're hurt at work, California law generally routes your claim through workers' compensation regardless of fault — but that's not always the whole story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate claim outside the workers' comp system. Santa Clara County work sites, from warehouses near US-101 to smaller commercial lots off Dunne Avenue, see their share of forklift accidents, falls, and vehicle-related injuries. Sorting out whether a third party is involved takes a careful look at how the injury happened. We can review the details of your case at no charge and explain what options might apply to your situation.
commonInjuries: Falls from ladders, scaffolding, or loading docks
Vehicle collisions while on the job or in company vehicles
Injuries from defective tools or machinery

whyChoose.title: Why Morgan Hill Injured Workers Choose Us

items.title: Understanding the 30-Day Reporting Window
items.desc: California requires injured workers to report the incident to their employer within 30 days to preserve workers' comp benefits. We can help make sure this step doesn't get missed or mishandled.

items.title: Spotting a Third-Party Claim
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, equipment maker, or other driver on the job site may open the door to a separate claim. We can evaluate whether that applies to your accident.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law prohibits employer retaliation against workers who report injuries or file claims. If you're worried about your job while recovering, we can explain your rights and the deadlines that protect them, including the 2-year window for third-party claims.

items.question: I was hurt at a warehouse near US-101 in Morgan Hill — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is your primary path against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. However, if a third party — like a delivery driver, contractor, or equipment supplier — contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate claim against them. We can look at the specifics and let you know which paths apply.

items.question: What if my employer says my injury doesn't qualify because I didn't report it right away?
items.answer: California generally requires injuries be reported within 30 days, so timing matters. That said, missing the exact date doesn't automatically end your options — we can review what happened and advise on next steps.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim in Morgan Hill?
items.answer: No — California law prohibits retaliation against employees for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, we can explain what protections and remedies may be available to you.
